problem: Audio-visual navigation (AVN) agents such as AV-NAV and AV-WaN overfit to the training sound types and generalise poorly to unheard sounds. Prior work only adds harder task settings (distractors, short sounds, multiple sources) or path planning, and none tackles this overfitting with the task unchanged.
motivation: A real agent must localise arbitrary sound sources, not just the few sounds heard in training. The audio encoder entangles sound category with source-receiver spatial information, so it fits training sounds. Regularising the encoder toward sound-agnostic, goal-driven features should improve generalisation without changing the task.
key_idea: Use a contrastive auxiliary loss (AFSO) that pulls together audio features of different sounds at the same source-receiver position and pushes apart features at different positions, plus sound reverse and mix-up augmentation.
insight: The encoder is forced to encode spatial relations rather than sound identity, and this plug-in gives about 12-13 points of SPL on both AV-NAV and AV-WaN on unseen scenes and unheard sounds. The paper reports no ablations separating AFSO from augmentation, so how much each part contributes is not shown. Positive pairs are cheap to build by re-convolving the same room impulse response with another sound, and the number of sampled audio observations N is kept small to limit false negatives.
method: AFSO auxiliary loss: SimCLR/InfoNCE contrastive loss on audio encoder features (cosine similarity, temperature 0.07), added to the standard AVN losses with weight w=0.1.

Positive pair simulation: for each binaural audio b_k, generate b~_k by convolving the current-step room impulse response with a different source sound, so the pair shares the same source-receiver geometry.
Negatives: all other samples in the batch of 2N (N originals plus N simulated) are negatives.

False-negative reduction: compute the loss only on a random subset of N=256 audio observations from the trajectories, since similar observations along a trajectory could otherwise be treated as negatives.
Sound Reverse augmentation: reverse the source audio signal with probability p=0.5 each episode.
Sound Mix-up augmentation: mix two (possibly reversed) sounds as λx1+(1-λ)x2, with λ~Beta(1,1).
Plug-in design: attached to existing frameworks (AV-NAV, AV-WaN) without changing the task definition.

setting.backbone: AV-NAV and AV-WaN audio-visual policies, retrained with the AFSO loss and augmentation, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces Replica and MP3D training scenes and sounds, plus simulated alternate-sound audio and reverse/mix-up augmented sounds
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D plus binaural audio spectrograms (AV-WaN also uses an occupancy map)
setting.action_space: AV-NAV: low-level discrete actions; AV-WaN: predicted waypoints on an occupancy map

numbers_note: Only one table, with no ablations. Benchmark is mapped to SoundSpaces (Replica and MP3D). The baselines are the authors' reproductions.
results: AFSO plus augmentation improves both baselines on unseen scenes with unheard sounds. AV-WaN on MP3D goes from SPL 36.2 to 48.4 and SR 57.4 to 73.9, and AV-NAV on Replica goes from SPL 38.2 to 51.4. Gains are about 12% SPL on both datasets.
limitations: No ablations separate the contribution of AFSO from the augmentations, and no hyperparameter sensitivity is reported.
Baselines are reproduced by the authors rather than taken from the original papers; the paper is a short workshop paper with a single table.
Positive pair simulation needs room impulse responses and a bank of alternative sounds, which limits the method to simulated training.
